title: Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat
abstract: Lean 4 proofs of the main results of Addario-Berry, Donderwinkel and Kortchemski, "Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat" (arXiv:2311.06163). For every critical offspring law, the height of the size-conditioned Bienaymé tree divided by log n tends to infinity and its width divided by n tends to zero in probability, along admissible sizes. These bounds are sharp: for every function f tending to infinity, a single critical offspring law has limsup P(height < f(n) log n) = 1 and limsup P(width > n/f(n)) = 1. For critical offspring laws in the local domain of attraction of the asymmetric Cauchy law (mu_n = L(n)/n^2 with L slowly varying), the height divided by an explicit scale h_n and the width divided by n E[Y 1{Y >= a_n}] both converge to 1 in probability, and height times width is O_P(n log n). The entry also includes the stochastic ordering of heights of uniform labelled trees with given degree sequences (Addario-Berry and Donderwinkel, Theorem 9), used in the paper. All 23 named results of the paper (its theorem, proposition, lemma and corollary environments) are proved in the repository; this Palomar entry compares the headline results.
